paras: Troubleshooting
Nothing happens
Start smaller:
“Show me one body sensation.” “Show me one word.” “Show me whether today is for listening or resting.”
It feels fake

What is it that feels fake? The words, an image, an expectation, a role? Be clear that not experiencing the inner voice/image is not, by itself, resistance or lack of adult capacity. If something is inviting you to do something you explicitly don’t want to do, correct it. It may also be a part that is protecting you, if so talk to it:

fixes.what: isn't, by itself, resistance
fixes.replace: is not a resistance
fixes.with: is not, by itself, resistance

paras: “What are you protecting me from?” or “Are you afraid I will lie to myself again?” or “Are you afraid this will just be a performance?”

It could be an inner voice of a parent you are picking up that is enforcing a rule about how you should be to belong, if so don’t argue with it, find out what rule it is enforcing and then work on finding ordinary evidence that would make your new adult voice more believable.

fixes.what: ordinary evidence that would make the adult voice more believable
fixes.replace: work on finding evidence to strengthen your new adult voice.
fixes.with: work on finding ordinary evidence that would make your new adult voice more believable.

paras: It may be that an adult capacity you need is not yet available to you, in that case stop trying to make yourself have an inner voice that you believe and if you have enough observing ego, borrow the warmth, boundary or direction you need from a caring someone (real or imagined) who has it. Try out one believable sentence or action etc and see how it goes.

fixes.what: the particular warmth, boundary or direction you lack; a caring figure; one believable sentence
fixes.replace: borrow the capacity you need from someone (real or imagined) who has it. Try out a sentence or action etc and see how it goes.
fixes.with: borrow the warmth, boundary or direction you need from a caring someone (real or imagined) who has it. Try out one believable sentence or action etc and see how it goes.

paras: The subconscious will not answer

There may not be an answer. There may not be a helpful answer. It may be that this isn’t a helpful question to ask at all, and you need to try a different one, or rest, or finish. But if you do sense that there’s something you need to consider about trust, what if you asked:
“What would you need to know in order to trust me?”

You might be surprised by how profoundly un-mystical the answer is. “I need to know you’ll set a boundary.” “I need to know you’ll follow through.” “I need to know you’ll stop leaving.” “I need to know you’ll stop putting insight in place of action.”

fixes.what: the fourth question: will you stop substituting insight for action
fixes.replace: “I need to know you’ll stop telling me that what I’m asking for isn’t actually what I need.”
fixes.with: “I need to know you’ll stop putting insight in place of action.”

paras: The inner child will not appear
If you can discern who the guard is, talk to it. If you can’t, then simply stay with the feeling or preference that’s actually there.

fixes.what: stay with the feeling or preference that is actually present (not 'talk in terms of')
fixes.replace: then simply talk in terms of your feelings or preferences.
fixes.with: then simply stay with the feeling or preference that’s actually there.

paras: “You don’t have to let me in. Just tell me what would make the doorway safer.”

fixes.what: the script: 'You do not have to let me in. Just tell me what would make the doorway safer.'
fixes.replace: “Even if you don’t let me in, there are things I can do to help you feel safer.”
fixes.with: “You don’t have to let me in. Just tell me what would make the doorway safer.”

paras: Even if there isn’t a clear child state to talk to, use the session to work with whatever you are aware of (a preference, curiosity, or a beginner’s experiment to try and see how it goes) instead of forcing an image. Building identity and reparenting can happen in the same practice.

fixes.what: a beginner experiment, instead of forcing an image
fixes.replace: by working with whatever you are aware of–preferences, curiosity, or even a statement that you’re new to this and would like to try something and see how it goes.
fixes.with: by working with whatever you are aware of (a preference, curiosity, or a beginner’s experiment to try and see how it goes) instead of forcing an image.

fixes.what: identity-building and reparenting can happen in the same practice (not 'reparenting by noticing preferences')
fixes.replace: you can still build identity and do reparenting by working with whatever you are aware of (a preference, curiosity, or a beginner’s experiment to try and see how it goes) instead of forcing an image.
fixes.with: use the session to work with whatever you are aware of (a preference, curiosity, or a beginner’s experiment to try and see how it goes) instead of forcing an image. Building identity and reparenting can happen in the same practice.

paras: You get anxious

Figure out whether your anxiety is manageable and you want to allow it to continue or whether you need less contact with it. If it’s escalating or overwhelming, stop searching for content and help your body first.

fixes.what: less contact (not 'do something to reduce it')
fixes.replace: or whether you need to do something to reduce it.
fixes.with: or whether you need less contact with it.

fixes.what: stop searching for content
fixes.replace: stop whatever you’re doing to help your body first.
fixes.with: stop searching for content and help your body first.

paras: Where are your feet? Your chair? Focus on your breath. Be with your body in the room.

Talk to your Little one and Protector parts: “Little one, I’m here for you. Protector, I know you’re trying to protect me. Thank you for letting me know. You don’t have to scream for me to listen. Do you need me to do something? If so, show me one step. If not, can you help my body stand down gently?”

fixes.what: 'You do not have to scream for me to listen'; show me one step; stand down gently
fixes.replace: Thank you for letting me know.
fixes.with: Thank you for letting me know. You don’t have to scream for me to listen.

fixes.what: show me one step
fixes.replace: If so, what?
fixes.with: If so, show me one step.

fixes.what: gently
fixes.replace: can you let my body know it can stand down?
fixes.with: can you help my body stand down gently?

fixes.what: 'Little'
fixes.replace: Talk to your Little and Protector parts:
fixes.with: Talk to your Little one and Protector parts:

For a longer list of ways to work with anxiety, see the toolbox in Appendix D.

fixes.replace: If your anxiety is causing you to have chest pain, faint, have suicidal thoughts, become psychotic or manic, severely dissociate, not sleep, or makes you want to hurt yourself or someone else, get help from a professional.
fixes.with: If your anxiety comes with chest pain, fainting, suicidal thoughts, psychosis-like or mania-like symptoms, severe dissociation or not being able to sleep, or makes you want to hurt yourself or someone else, get help from a professional.

paras: You become too analytical
Stop trying to do the practice better. Put one hand on your heart and one on your solar plexis and say,
“I’m not here to do this perfectly. I’m here to be in relationship with what’s deeper than my surface mind.”
“What would help me turn this into a communion rather than a performance?”
Sometimes the answer is to be silent, to rest, to do one honest thing. Do the thing that comes to you.

fixes.replace: “I’m not supposed to be doing this well.
fixes.with: “I’m not here to do this perfectly.

fixes.what: the script lost its closing quotation mark
fixes.replace: deeper than my surface mind.
fixes.with: deeper than my surface mind.”

fixes.what: one honest action
fixes.replace: to do something.
fixes.with: to do one honest thing.

fixes.what: here to be in relationship (not 'supposed to be entering')
fixes.replace: I’m supposed to be entering into relationship
fixes.with: I’m here to be in relationship

paras: You become too blissful or diffuse
Bring it down to a specific level.
“What task, boundary, meal, rest, repair, or conversation does love need from me right now?”

fixes.what: the script's list: what task, boundary, meal, rest, repair or conversation
fixes.replace: “What would love do right now?”
fixes.with: “What task, boundary, meal, rest, repair, or conversation does love need from me right now?”

paras: You want the hidden truth immediately
Refrain. Say, “First show me the capacity, and you can show me the content later.”
You keep daydreaming
Sit up and open your eyes. Then ask, “What real action am I avoiding with this fantasy?”
You get stuck in spiritual bypass
Ask, “Where is divine love not yet descending to meet my pain?”

You may have had a genuinely profound opening that revealed to you how much more love and freedom are possible. Let that matter, without demanding that the child receive it on command. It’s also possible that prayer left you feeling abandoned or condemned, or that a teacher’s betrayal damaged something sacred. It’s worth asking what was lost and what needs questioning. But doing more of the same may not be the answer.

Sometimes practical care helps while the horizon of your life still feels too small, and to follow your curiosity about deeper happiness without pretending to believe an explanation. Some people already have enough love and meaning for the life they want. Spirituality doesn’t have to be another thing you’re supposed to do.

fixes.what: let that matter without demanding the child receive it on command
fixes.replace: how much more love and freedom are possible.
fixes.with: how much more love and freedom are possible. Let that matter, without demanding that the child receive it on command.

fixes.what: 'as a child, you prayed'; the published: prayer can evoke abandonment or condemnation, or a teacher's betrayal can damage something sacred
fixes.replace: It’s also possible that, as a child, you prayed and then felt abandoned or condemned; that you went to a teacher and were betrayed.
fixes.with: It’s also possible that prayer left you feeling abandoned or condemned, or that a teacher’s betrayal damaged something sacred.

fixes.replace: It’s worth asking some questions about what happened.
fixes.with: It’s worth asking what was lost and what needs questioning.

fixes.with: Sometimes the best thing is to do something practical in your life while the horizon still feels too small, and to follow your curiosity about deeper happiness without pretending to believe an explanation.

paras: You get stuck in endless processing

You may have a real wound to deal with, but you may also have a checking loop. Ask yourself, “Does this round help me feel, understand, decide or respond differently, or am I checking again for reassurance?” Sometimes, both in grieving and in practice, it’s fine to cover the same ground again; it doesn’t have to be new every time.

If you discover that you are in a checking loop, then let the thought be there but don’t argue with it or chase it away. Return to some chosen activity or relationship. You don’t have to hold a meeting with every thought that arises. You don’t have to complete some ritual before you can start your life.
Ask yourself, “What direction would the Leader choose now?”

fixes.what: does this round help you feel, understand, decide or respond differently, or are you checking for reassurance
fixes.replace: “Am I looking for something new here, or am I checking again to see if it’s gone yet?”
fixes.with: “Does this round help me feel, understand, decide or respond differently, or am I checking again for reassurance?”

fixes.replace: you’re supposed to cover the same ground over and over again.
fixes.with: it’s fine to cover the same ground again; it doesn’t have to be new every time.

fixes.what: or chasing it away
fixes.replace: but don’t argue with it.
fixes.with: but don’t argue with it or chase it away.

fixes.what: complete a ritual (not 'some magical thing')
fixes.replace: You don’t have to do some magical thing before you can start your life.
fixes.with: You don’t have to complete some ritual before you can start your life.

fixes.what: the Leader's question: what direction, now
fixes.replace: “What would the Leader do?”
fixes.with: “What direction would the Leader choose now?”
